column1:
The FOMC statement’s tone is mildly constructive—solid labor market, firming business investment, and a transitory view of Q1 softness—while inflation is still somewhat below 2% and policy remains accommodative and data dependent.

April 2017 SLOOS adds a mixed-but-leaning-easy credit backdrop: domestic banks eased some C&I terms citing a better economic outlook and showed greater willingness to lend to consumer installment/credit card borrowers, but tightened standards for auto loans and expressed pockets of caution around CRE (less favorable vacancy/property-price outlook; concerns about securitization). Foreign banks reported higher loan-rate spreads and lower LTVs, and banks noted regulatory/liquidity/capital considerations. This points to generally supportive credit supply with selective tightening and elevated caution in rate‑sensitive and CRE segments.

Net effect: still positive, but SLOOS tempers the optimism a bit more than before, warranting a slightly lower score. sentiment score = 0.15
